note: Five dual PI3K/mTOR inhibitors reached breast cancer patients on xenograft tumour-stasis data; the one phase 2 that read out (voxtalisib plus letrozole) found no responses, dactolisib never found a tolerable regimen, and the other three were dropped before any breast efficacy endpoint.
label: Breast cancer (PI3K/mTOR)

engagement.model: Novartis BEZ235 xenografts with ex-vivo tumour PI3K/Akt pathway readout
engagement.note: Tumour PI3K/Akt pathway inhibition tracked BEZ235 concentration ex vivo in xenografts; no patient readout existed yet.
engagement.short: Tumour pAkt tracks BEZ235 exposure in mice
engagement.quote: Ex vivo pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic analyses of tumor tissues showed a time-dependent correlation between compound concentration and PI3K/Akt pathway inhibition.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; xenograft lines not named in the abstract.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry: the model's PD readout is tumour pAkt/pS6, which is what the phase I later biopsied.

engagement.model: Novartis BEZ235 xenografts with ex-vivo tumour PI3K/Akt pathway readout
engagement.note: Paired tumour biopsies in three dactolisib patients showed pS6 down a median 23% (range 15-59%), the direction the xenografts gave.
engagement.short: pS6 fell in three patient biopsies
engagement.quote: Data from paired tumor biopsies at cycle 1 day 28, in three patients treated with HGC formulation showed a decrease in pS6 levels from baseline with a median decrease of − 23.08% (range − 59.2 to − 15.0).
engagement.reason: Tumour pS6 fell as in xenografts
engagement.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC6286256). Only three paired biopsies, all on the hard-gelatin-capsule formulation that was dropped for low exposure; no numeric model-side effect to scale against.
engagement.judgement: Direction matched (pathway phosphoprotein down in dosed patients), so same at low confidence; n=3 and the paper says no biomarker correlated with response. pS6 is scored proximal because it is the direct product of mTORC1, one of the two targets. The HER2+ breast cohort itself had no biopsy PD readout reported.
engagement.population: advanced solid tumours, single-agent dose escalation

engagement.model: Exelixis XL765 xenograft panel with dose-dependent pAKT/p70S6K/S6 inhibition
engagement.note: XL765 cut pAKT, p70S6K and pS6 in xenograft tumours for about 24 h after an oral dose.
engagement.quote: In mouse xenograft models, oral administration of XL765 results in dose-dependent inhibition of phosphorylation of AKT, p70S6K, and S6 with a duration of action of approximately 24 hours.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The Exelixis characterisation paper was published in 2014, after the first-in-human study (2007-), so model_first_use_year is the publication year, not the compound's first use.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry for the voxtalisib track; the model's readout is tumour pathway phosphoproteins.

engagement.model: Exelixis XL765 xenograft panel with dose-dependent pAKT/p70S6K/S6 inhibition
engagement.note: Voxtalisib 50 mg BID inhibited PI3K/mTOR and ERK signalling in the tumour of one responding lymphoma patient; breast trial PD was glucose only.
engagement.short: Pathway inhibition in one patient tumour
engagement.quote: In a patient with mantle cell lymphoma achieving PR, SAR245409 was associated with significant inhibition of PI3K/mTOR and extracellular signal-related kinase
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (paywalled); the quote is a verbatim leading fragment of the abstract's PD sentence. One patient, lymphoma not breast; epub 2014-11-19 sets the year, print 2015.
engagement.judgement: Engagement admits any dosed human, so the lymphoma expansion cohort counts; direction matched in one tumour, hence same at low confidence. Blackwell 2015 reported only glucose homeostasis (a downstream readout) for the breast combination and found voxtalisib's PD impact weaker than pilaralisib's, which is why confidence stays low rather than medium.

engagement.model: Genentech GDC-0980 PI3K-pathway-activated xenografts with exposure-linked PD biomarkers
engagement.note: GDC-0980 gave exposure-related PD biomarker decreases in PI3K-activated, LKB1- or PTEN-null xenografts.
engagement.quote: Low doses of GDC-0980 potently inhibited tumor growth in xenograft models including those with activated PI3K, loss of LKB1 or PTEN, and elicited an exposure-related decrease in PD biomarkers.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the abstract names breast among the most sensitive cell-line lineages but not the xenograft lines.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry for the apitolisib track.

engagement.model: Genentech GDC-0980 PI3K-pathway-activated xenografts with exposure-linked PD biomarkers
engagement.note: Apitolisib suppressed pAKT S473 by at least 90% in platelet-rich plasma at the MTD and cut FDG uptake over 25% in 66% at 40 mg.
engagement.short: pAKT down 90% in patients at MTD
engagement.quote: Phosphorylated serine-473 AKT levels were suppressed by ≥90% in platelet-rich plasma within 4 hours at the MTD (50 mg).
engagement.reason: Dose-related pAKT suppression held in patients
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; PRP pAKT is a surrogate tissue, not tumour, and the model side gives no number to scale against.
engagement.judgement: Wallin's exposure-related PD decrease reproduced in dosed patients (target modulation from 16 mg, 90% pAKT S473 suppression at the MTD), so same; pAKT S473 is mTORC2's direct product, hence proximal. Mixed solid-tumour phase I, admissible for engagement. Comparison is my pairing, not stated.
engagement.magnitude_basis: pAKT S473 suppression in platelet-rich plasma

engagement.model: Genentech translational PK/PD-efficacy model of apitolisib (xenograft pAkt-to-tumour-growth link with allometric human PK)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Drug Metab Dispos, not in PMC). 2012 is a publication proxy: the prediction was made before first-in-human dosing (NCT00854152 started 2009-03). Apitolisib never reached an NDA, so model_filed is unknown.
engagement.quote: Parameters estimated from the pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic modeling of the MCF7-neo/HER2 xenograft data indicated that the GDC-0980 plasma concentration required for tumor stasis was approximately 0.5 μM.
engagement.note: Mouse PK/PD model tied tumour pAkt suppression to MCF7-neo/HER2 stasis at about 0.5 µM; no human PD comparison yet.
engagement.short: Xenograft pAkt-to-stasis model, untested in humans
engagement.judgement: Opens the in-silico track. The PK/PD model is a different system from the Wallin 2011 efficacy panel: it predicts a quantitative human exposure, clearance and dose, which the xenograft panel does not.

engagement.model: Genentech translational PK/PD-efficacy model of apitolisib (xenograft pAkt-to-tumour-growth link with allometric human PK)
engagement.magnitude_basis: constant pAkt inhibition needed for tumour stasis: 61% in 786-O xenografts vs 65% in phase 1 patients (platelet-rich plasma); 35-45% threshold in both
engagement.population: Advanced solid tumour phase 1 patients (NCT00854152, NCT00854126), 2-200 mg; not breast-specific
engagement.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC11315854). Both integrated models were fit in 2024 to phase 1 data public since Dolly 2016, so this is a retrodiction. Patients were mixed solid tumours, admitted under engagement's any-dosed-human rule. The concentration-to-pAkt IC50 differed 43-fold between tumour tissue (403 µg/L) and plasma (9.32 µg/L), which the authors attribute to matrix. Neither phase 1 posted registry results.
engagement.quote: Based on this relationship between targeted pAkt modulation and tumor shrinkage rate, it appeared that a constant pAkt inhibition of 61% and 65%, respectively, would be necessary to achieve tumor stasis in xenografts and patients.
engagement.note: Retrospective integrated PK-PD-efficacy models fit to xenograft and phase 1 data gave the same steep pAkt-to-tumour-shrinkage curve and stasis threshold.
engagement.short: Xenograft pAkt-efficacy curve reproduced in patients
engagement.judgement: Retro, not same: the clinical model was built after the phase 1 answer was known (decision 10). Direction and the stasis threshold agree within 2x; the 43-fold IC50 gap sits in the concentration-to-pAkt link, so the source's own framing is partial.

dose.model: Novartis BEZ235 xenografts with ex-vivo tumour PI3K/Akt pathway readout
dose.note: Oral BEZ235 gave disease stasis in xenografts and was stated to be well tolerated at those doses.
dose.short: Stasis at tolerated oral doses in mice
dose.quote: Thus, the compound was well tolerated, displayed disease stasis when administered orally, and enhanced the efficacy of other anticancer agents when used in in vivo combination studies.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the tolerated/effective mouse doses are not in the abstract.
dose.judgement: Opening entry; the model states a tolerability margin at the effective regimen, which is what decision 16 scores later.

dose.model: Novartis BEZ235 xenografts with ex-vivo tumour PI3K/Akt pathway readout
dose.note: Exposure CV above 100% at 100 mg and up; nausea 80%, diarrhoea 75% set the MTD; the breast phase Ib/II with paclitaxel could not set a dose.
dose.short: No tolerable regimen reached exposure target
dose.quote: Pharmacokinetic profiles showed low-to-moderate variability at low dose (10 mg) and high variability at high doses (100 mg and above). Gastrointestinal AEs were frequent at high doses.
dose.reason: GI toxicity blocked the mouse regimen
dose.confidence_note: Full text read. The paper never states the preclinical efficacious exposure or whether the MTD reached it, and attributes the GI toxicity to precipitation of the drug at high doses rather than mechanism; three formulations were tried. NCT01495247 (BEZ235 + paclitaxel, HER2-negative breast) is terminated with 'did not meet Phase Ib primary objective to establish the maximum tolerated dose/recommended dose for Phase II' and no posted results; its termination date is not retrievable from the registry record.
dose.judgement: Decision 16: the model stated the effective regimen was tolerated; in patients the continuous daily regimen was limited by GI toxicity with >100% exposure variability, dactolisib with trastuzumab stopped at 600 mg/day, and the breast phase Ib/II could not set a dose, so the harm is counted here as a misplaced margin and not in safety. A reviewer who weighs the formulation explanation could call this untested (no exposure comparison published); I score the regimen, which the mouse said was tolerable and the clinic could not deliver. Efficacy on this track therefore stays untested.
dose.population: advanced solid tumours incl. HER2-positive breast cancer with trastuzumab

dose.model: Exelixis XL765 xenograft panel with dose-dependent pAKT/p70S6K/S6 inhibition
dose.note: The model's regimen target was pathway inhibition lasting about 24 h after each oral dose.
dose.short: 24 h pathway inhibition per dose in mice
dose.quote: In mouse xenograft models, oral administration of XL765 results in dose-dependent inhibition of phosphorylation of AKT, p70S6K, and S6 with a duration of action of approximately 24 hours.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; no tolerability statement in the abstract, so margin_stated is false.
dose.judgement: Opening entry for the voxtalisib track.

dose.model: Genentech GDC-0980 PI3K-pathway-activated xenografts with exposure-linked PD biomarkers
dose.note: Low xenograft doses sufficed; Dolly 2016 found target modulation from 16 mg and an RP2D of 40 mg, but no breast trial read out to say whether it was enough.
dose.short: Target reached in phase I, never tested in breast
dose.quote: Low doses of GDC-0980 potently inhibited tumor growth in xenograft models including those with activated PI3K, loss of LKB1 or PTEN, and elicited an exposure-related decrease in PD biomarkers.
dose.reason: No breast efficacy to judge enough
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of both papers. FERGI arm B (apitolisib 30 mg + fulvestrant, NCT01437566) completed in 2016 without posted results or a publication I could find, so 'reached and enough' cannot be judged.
dose.judgement: Half the dose question (reached) is answered by Dolly 2016 in solid tumours, the other half (enough) needs a breast efficacy readout that was never published, so the track stays untested rather than same.

dose.model: Genentech translational PK/PD-efficacy model of apitolisib (xenograft pAkt-to-tumour-growth link with allometric human PK)
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Drug Metab Dispos, not in PMC). 2012 is a publication proxy: the prediction was made before first-in-human dosing (NCT00854152 started 2009-03). Apitolisib never reached an NDA, so model_filed is unknown.
dose.quote: These parameters, combined with the predicted human pharmacokinetic profile, suggested that 55 mg once daily may be a clinically efficacious dose.
dose.note: Allometry predicted human CL 5.1 mL/min/kg and 55 mg once daily as the efficacious dose; no tolerability margin stated.
dose.reason: 55 mg never tolerated; no stated margin
dose.judgement: Later knowledge recorded without changing status: Dolly 2016 (doi 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-15-2225) found MTD 50 mg and RP2D 40 mg once daily with fasting hyperglycaemia dose-limiting at 40 and 70 mg, and Moein 2024 population CL/F of 0.304 L/h/kg (5.07 mL/min/kg) matched the 5.1 mL/min/kg prediction. The predicted regimen was never a tolerated dose and the model stated no margin, so decision 16's no-margin row keeps the cell untested rather than contra with blocked_by toxicity.

efficacy.model: Novartis BEZ235 xenografts with ex-vivo tumour PI3K/Akt pathway readout
efficacy.note: BEZ235 reversed PTEN-loss and PIK3CA-mutant lapatinib resistance in HER2+ breast models; no breast trial ever read a primary efficacy endpoint.
efficacy.short: PI3K-altered HER2+ models respond; no trial readout
efficacy.quote: Furthermore, we show that phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)-induced lapatinib resistance can be abrogated through the use of NVP-BEZ235, a dual inhibitor of PI3K/mTOR.

patient_trials.quote: Thirty patients with HER2+ aBC received BEZ235 in combination with trastuzumab. The MTD of BEZ235 in combination with trastuzumab was 600 mg/day. A total of four patients (13.3%) achieved partial response across the different groups.
Study did not meet Phase Ib primary objective to establish the maximum tolerated dose/recommended dose for Phase II

efficacy.reason: No breast primary efficacy endpoint read
efficacy.confidence_note: Eichhorn 2008 read at abstract level; Rodon 2018 full text. None of the four breast registrations posted results; NCT01471847 (phase Ib/II with trastuzumab, PFS primary) enrolled 5 and NCT01495247 was terminated without an RP2D, so no phase II started.
efficacy.judgement: The only breast efficacy data are 4/30 partial responses (DCR 47%) in a phase Ib cohort of PI3K-pathway-altered HER2+ patients whose primary endpoint was DLT, so the efficacy question is unscored; under the dose table (target blocked by toxicity) it stays untested. Eichhorn's patient-level prediction is consistent with those responses but was never tested on an efficacy endpoint.

efficacy.model: Exelixis XL765 xenograft panel with dose-dependent pAKT/p70S6K/S6 inhibition
efficacy.note: Repeat oral XL765 gave significant tumour growth inhibition across xenografts, with genotype affecting cell-line sensitivity.
efficacy.quote: Repeat dose administration of XL765 results in significant tumor growth inhibition in multiple human xenograft models in nude mice that is associated with antiproliferative, antiangiogenic, and proapoptotic effects.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the breast xenografts in the panel are not named in the abstract.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry; the prediction is tumour growth inhibition, with a secondary patient-level claim that PI3K-pathway genotype shapes sensitivity.

efficacy.model: Exelixis XL765 xenograft panel with dose-dependent pAKT/p70S6K/S6 inhibition
efficacy.note: Phase II voxtalisib plus letrozole: no partial responses, 6-month PFS 8%, no link between PI3K-pathway alterations and benefit.
efficacy.short: No responses, PFS6 8% in phase II
efficacy.quote: In summary, pilaralisib or voxtalisib, in combination with letrozole, was associated with an acceptable safety profile and limited efficacy in endocrine therapy-resistant HR+ , HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer.

patient_trials.quote: Fifty-one patients were enrolled in phase II; one patient had a partial response in the pilaralisib arm. Rates of progression-free survival at 6 months were 17 and 8 % in the pilaralisib and voxtalisib arms, respectively.

efficacy.reason: Xenograft growth inhibition, no patient benefit
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (paywalled). The registry's phase II primary is PFS at 3 months; the abstract reports PFS at 6 months (8%) and no responders in the voxtalisib arm. No results posted on NCT01082068.
efficacy.judgement: Class-level miss: the xenografts predicted growth inhibition and the HR+/HER2-negative phase II found no responses and PFS6 of 8% with letrozole, which the sponsor did not pursue. The patient-level claim also failed ('no association between molecular alterations in the PI3K pathway and efficacy'). Pairing of Yu 2014 with the trial is mine; the trial does not cite the model. Only member with a breast phase II readout, so this entry sets the class cell; neg is unreachable because the model data for voxtalisib were not below the class bar.
efficacy.population: HR-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer refractory to a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor

efficacy.model: Genentech GDC-0980 PI3K-pathway-activated xenografts with exposure-linked PD biomarkers
efficacy.note: Breast lines were among the most sensitive; the apitolisib arm of FERGI (PFS primary) finished in 2016 with nothing published.
efficacy.quote: Correspondingly, GDC-0980 was potent across a broad panel of cancer cell lines, with the greatest potency in breast, prostate, and lung cancers and less activity in melanoma and pancreatic cancers, consistent with KRAS and BRAF acting as resistance markers.
efficacy.reason: Breast arm completed, results never published
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. NCT01437566 lists arm B (GDC-0980 30 mg + fulvestrant) against a shared placebo arm with PFS primary, completed 2016-04, no posted results; the FERGI publication I know of (Krop 2016) covers pictilisib only. NCT01254526 (apitolisib + paclitaxel ± bevacizumab, n=52) likewise unpublished.
efficacy.judgement: A model existed and a breast trial ran, but no admissible comparison exists, so untested, not an empty cell.

efficacy.model: Pfizer PF-04691502 PTEN-null and PIK3CA-mutant xenografts
efficacy.note: Xenograft activity in PTEN-null and PIK3CA-mutant lines, none breast; the pre-operative letrozole trial was stopped before its Ki-67 endpoint.
efficacy.short: Pre-op trial stopped before Ki-67 readout
efficacy.quote: Antitumor activity was observed in U87 (PTEN null), SKOV3 (PIK3CA mutation), and gefitinib- and erlotinib-resistant non-small cell lung carcinoma xenografts.

patient_trials.quote: The study was prematurely discontinued on 09Oct2012 due to the tolerability findings in 2 clinical studies testing PF-04691502 that have prompted the Sponsor to re-evaluate the strategic goals of the program.

efficacy.reason: Program stopped before any efficacy endpoint
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Yuan 2011; registry record NCT01430585 read in full (results posted 2014-08-12: 14 phase 1b patients, phase 2 Ki-67 arms empty). NCT01658176 (with exemestane) was withdrawn.
efficacy.judgement: No breast comparison is possible: the only breast trial ended in its phase 1b after Pfizer saw severe skin toxicity in another study, so untested with the registry record kept as the patient-side trail.

efficacy.model: PIQUR PQR309 tumour cell lines and rat xenograft
efficacy.note: A rat xenograft carried bimiralisib to the clinic; the HER2-negative breast trial with eribulin completed in 2018 without published results.
efficacy.quote: Compound 1 demonstrated efficiency in inhibiting proliferation in tumor cell lines and a rat xenograft model.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. PIQHASSO (NCT02723877, n=41, clinical benefit rate co-primary) completed 2018-10-03 with no posted results; a PubMed search for PIQHASSO or bimiralisib + eribulin returned nothing, and I did not search conference abstracts or press releases.
efficacy.judgement: Model existed, trial ran, no comparison published: untested.

efficacy.model: Genentech translational PK/PD-efficacy model of apitolisib (xenograft pAkt-to-tumour-growth link with allometric human PK)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Drug Metab Dispos, not in PMC). 2012 is a publication proxy: the prediction was made before first-in-human dosing (NCT00854152 started 2009-03). Apitolisib never reached an NDA, so model_filed is unknown.
efficacy.quote: Parameters estimated from the pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic modeling of the MCF7-neo/HER2 xenograft data indicated that the GDC-0980 plasma concentration required for tumor stasis was approximately 0.5 μM.
efficacy.note: Model predicted tumour stasis at 55 mg once daily; FERGI arm B and the paclitaxel combination never reported a breast endpoint.
efficacy.judgement: The stasis prediction came from an MCF7-neo/HER2 breast xenograft, so it bears on this tile, but the only breast trials (NCT01437566 arm B, NCT01254526) completed without results and the 55 mg regimen was never given, so nothing can be scored.

safety.model: Novartis BEZ235 xenografts with ex-vivo tumour PI3K/Akt pathway readout
safety.note: The model said well tolerated; the GI harm that broke that is counted in dose, and class harms (hyperglycaemia, rash, pneumonitis) were not prevalent.
safety.short: GI harm counted in dose cell
safety.quote: Thus, the compound was well tolerated, displayed disease stasis when administered orally, and enhanced the efficacy of other anticancer agents when used in in vivo combination studies.
safety.confidence_note: Rodon 2018 full text: 'hyperglycemia and rash ... and pneumonitis ... were not prevalent in this study'; stomatitis near everolimus rates. Abstract-level for the model.
safety.judgement: Decision 16 puts the tolerability miss in dose (stated margin, misplaced), so safety is not double-counted. A reviewer could score the absence of the class harms as same with source_calls_it partial; I left it untested because the model made no harm-specific prediction to hold.

safety.model: Genentech GDC-0980 PI3K-pathway-activated xenografts with exposure-linked PD biomarkers
safety.note: Efficacy paper; no tolerability, glucose or lung finding in the abstract.
safety.quote: Low doses of GDC-0980 potently inhibited tumor growth in xenograft models including those with activated PI3K, loss of LKB1 or PTEN, and elicited an exposure-related decrease in PD biomarkers.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the full text may report mouse glucose or weight, which would change the next entry from silence to a stated margin.
safety.judgement: Opening entry: no safety statement in the abstract.

safety.model: Genentech GDC-0980 PI3K-pathway-activated xenografts with exposure-linked PD biomarkers
safety.note: Fasting hyperglycaemia was dose-limiting at 40 and 70 mg and pneumonitis hit 8% at RP2D; mice show PI3K-inhibitor hyperglycaemia and the model was silent.
safety.quote: Dose-limiting toxicities (1 patient each) were G4 fasting hyperglycemia at 40 mg (21/28 schedule) and G3 maculopapular rash and G3 fasting hyperglycemia at 70 mg (21/28 schedule).
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level on both sides. The comparison is imported from a mixed solid-tumour phase I (no breast safety readout for apitolisib exists). If Wallin 2011's full text reports mouse glucose, this becomes a predicted harm and belongs in dose as a margin call, not here.
safety.judgement: On-target hyperglycaemia is a harm mice can show (PI3K inhibition raises glucose in mice), so the model's silence is scored as contradicted; pneumonitis is left out of the call because rodents do not reliably show mTOR-inhibitor pneumonitis. Class-consistent: bimiralisib hyperglycaemia in at least 30% with a G3 hyperglycaemia DLT (Wicki 2018) and voxtalisib glucose effects (Blackwell 2015). Dactolisib's track differs: its class harms were not prevalent, so no contra is drawn there.
